The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=-2$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=2.$

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=-4$ and $x=0.$*

${f}^{′}(-2)≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 
at the point $x=-2$ with step size $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(-2) & ≈\frac{f(-2+2)-f(-2-2)}{2(2)} \\  & =\frac{f(0)-f(-4)}{4} \\  & =\frac{5-1}{4} \\  & =\frac{4}{4} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
